title: Winota vs Winota vs Winota vs Winota | CEDH Gameplay #179
era_note: 2022 game under the pre-2024 Commander banlist and meta: Dockside Extortionist, Mana Crypt, and Jeweled Lotus (all central to these games) were legal then and are banned as of Sept 2024. Treat win speeds as 2022-meta data.

players.note: all four seats play Winota, Joiner of Forces; names spoken by the announcer every turn and confirmed against on-screen overlays via frame sampling 2026-08-24 (Mike top-left, Lua top-right, Ian bottom-left, Rachel bottom-right; overlay shows per-player life and a round counter)

decklists.list_fidelity_warning: Five cards seen or named in the video are absent from the corresponding provided list (see known_list_divergences); the provided lists appear to be later or reconstructed versions, not the exact 2022 lists.

extraction.method: manual LLM read of the transcript (data/transcripts/OuY6mdiXbHU.txt) plus targeted video frame sampling (yt-dlp --download-sections + ffmpeg stills) for seat overlays, life totals, round counter, and both game endings
caveats: This transcript is scripted announcer narration of an edited recap, not raw table audio: card names are clean (zero garbled-name repairs needed) but off-camera details and any un-narrated plays are invisible.

The channel shows each opening hand and lists 'London Mulligans' separately; interpreted as the cards bottomed under the London rule, so cards kept = 7 minus bottomed. This interpretation is corroborated by Mike's game 2 (4 bottomed = kept 3, and he takes almost no game actions all game) but is itself an inference.
Overlay round counter counts table rounds, not player-turns; win_turn_estimate below is the winner's own elapsed/active turn, with the round counter noted separately.

first_commander_turn.note: turn-1 Winota by Rachel in game 1 via SSG + Chrome Mox + Sol Ring + Mana Vault + Dockside treasures

headline_features.mull_aggression: game 2 was won off a keep of 4; Mike kept 3 in game 2 and was a non-participant, corroborating the mulligan interpretation
headline_features.interaction_density: very low by cEDH standards: zero counterspells resolved across both games; interaction was flash blockers, protection activations, one evoked Solitude (fizzled), and stax bodies
headline_features.mirror_dynamics: all four decks race the same plan; the winner both games was the player whose Winota triggers connected earliest and most often, plus the incidental lifegain (Rick + Blade Historian) that put game 1 out of reach

open_questions: Are the four provided decklists the players' actual September 2022 lists? Five in-video cards are missing from them, so they read as later or reconstructed versions; win-condition and mana-base cores match, but exact-card replay fidelity is not guaranteed.
Game 1 win is a concession to inevitability, not a demonstrated kill; whether Lua had guaranteed lethal on her turn 4 is unverifiable, so the round-4 figure is a concession round, not a combo round.
The recap is edited; any plays the editor cut (for example incidental treasure cracks or land drops) are invisible, though the narration style suggests near-complete coverage.
